clue.text: Mission endlessly restricted by alien vehicle returning with a new secret

indicators.note: the shortened mission word is held in, restricted, by the reversed alien vehicle
returning means the alien and the vehicle are read backwards together

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial
a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for mission is cut off

parts.note: an errand is a mission

explanation.surface: A secret new mission is being hampered by an alien spacecraft coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal signal, 'returning', turns the alien and vehicle together, giving SUBTE as a single unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something subterranean is underground, hence hidden or clandestine.

clue.text: Exhibitionist's problem

definitions.meaning: one who strikes attitudes to show off

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off who strikes attitudes and a tricky question share this one word.

clue.text: Bugs in system, tons left, freeze

parts.note: a plan is a system or scheme
ice, as a verb, means freeze

explanation.surface: Bugs in a computer system cause failures; tons of data left frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are small sap-sucking insects, and bugs is a general word for insects.

clue.text: American endeavour after difficulty losing breadth and diligence

indicators.note: after places the American abbreviation behind the shortened difficulty
losing means the letter for breadth is taken away from the difficulty word

parts.note: a bind is a difficulty or nuisance
a try is an endeavour or attempt

explanation.surface: American effort that follows hardship, minus breadth, shows diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing breadth' takes B from BIND, leaving IND.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in its older sense is hard work, synonymous with diligence.

clue.text: Ruffian repelled old man before long

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the word for old man is read in reverse

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
to ache is to long or yearn; the before puts it after the reversed father

explanation.surface: A thug rebuffed his father before pining for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An apache was a Parisian street ruffian or gangster, named after the Native American people.

clue.text: Bird in group with hesitant utterance falling back, looking sickly

indicators.note: falling back means the group and the utterance are read backwards together

parts.note: a set is a group
um is a hesitant noise in speech
wan means pale, looking sickly

explanation.surface: A bird in a flock stammers, retreats and looks unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling back' turns SET + UM into MUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is a common European species of swan, a large water bird.

clue.text: Take off when clubs close

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
close as a noun means end

explanation.surface: Take off when the clubs shut for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise up, as a plane does when taking off.

clue.text: Relaxing before noon in nest

indicators.note: in means the morning abbreviation is placed inside the nest word

parts.note: a drey is a squirrel's nest
AM means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Relaxing in the nest before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy music or atmosphere is soothing, relaxing.

clue.text: Vision changed with involvement of church in accounts

indicators.note: involvement means the church abbreviation is rolled into the middle of the rearranged letters
changed signals the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A new vision for the accounts, with the church getting involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' gives INVOIS, which the church abbreviation enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Invoices are bills, itemised accounts sent for payment.

clue.text: Success dividing river, permitting passage in opposite directions

indicators.note: dividing means the success word splits the river name in two

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
a wow is a big hit, a success

explanation.surface: A triumph splits the river, letting traffic go both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-way street or valve lets movement occur both ways.

clue.text: Hired clerk's wife with note Pole tossed around

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: around means the pole goes round the wife letter

parts.note: a caber is a pole tossed at Highland games

explanation.surface: A clerk's wife and a Polish man thrown about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' wants a Polish person; it is the caber tossed at Scottish Highland games. Mr Micawber is hired as clerk by Uriah Heep in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: In David Copperfield the impecunious Wilkins character is taken on as Heep's clerk.

clue.text: Possibility about diet and nuts

parts.note: ca, for circa, means about

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Perhaps some hopeful about diets and nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is a possible choice, one in the running.

clue.text: Trace element, germanium

parts.note: tin is a chemical element
Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium

explanation.surface: A trace element, germanium, found in a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour or quality.

clue.text: Cheat, one sure to win power, yearning in state of readiness

parts.note: to con is to cheat
a cert is a racing term for a certainty, one sure to win
an itch is a yearning or craving

explanation.surface: A swindler, a sure winner, power and longing combine in readiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert pitch figuratively means full readiness, from tuning instruments to the standard pitch.

clue.text: Work to stop separation, ignoring constant illogical argument

indicators.note: to stop means the work word plugs a gap in the middle of the other word
ignoring means the letter for constant is left out

parts.note: a schism is a split or separation
C is the scientific symbol for a constant (the speed of light)
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Work intended to stop a split, but neglecting the constant, is faulty reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring constant' leaves SHISM for the work to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophism is a clever but fallacious argument.

clue.text: Irrelevant aspect in opinion with pith one demolished

indicators.note: in means the aspect word goes inside the opinion word

parts.note: 'my bet is' means my opinion is
a side is an aspect

indicators.note: demolished means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irrelevant aspect of an opinion with its core knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opinion' is BET as in 'my bet is'; 'demolished' rearranges the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off the topic under discussion, so of no relevance.

clue.text: Attention non-smoker gains

parts.note: to give ear is to give attention
NS is the abbreviation for non-smoker

explanation.surface: A non-smoker gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain, as of money or merit.

clue.text: Hastened to protect most of capital after start of investigation of bank

indicators.note: to protect means the hastened word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: ran means hastened

indicators.note: after places the shortened capital behind the opening letter
start of means take the first letter of investigation
most of means the last letter of the capital is dropped

parts.note: Paris is a capital city

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to shield the capital after an investigation into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial; it is a riverbank. 'most of' trims PARIS to PARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Riparian means relating to or living on the banks of a river.

clue.text: Interact with odd characters discharged in good order

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are thrown out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Get along with strange people being let go in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy, everything in its place.

clue.text: Opponent finished old course

parts.note: an anti is someone opposed
past means over, finished

explanation.surface: An opponent who completed an old racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is an Italian starter, the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Check bait in crooked trap for unofficial advisers

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Check the bait in the bent trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns CHECK BAIT IN into KITCHENCABI.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cabinet is an informal group of advisers close to a leader, outside the official cabinet.

clue.text: Layer cut by man with large saw

indicators.note: cut by means the layer word is split open by the other pieces

parts.note: a bed is a layer, as of rock
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A layer cut by a man with a big saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a tool; it is the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to see.

clue.text: Likeable rascal in funny cast I love

indicators.note: in means the rascal word goes inside the rearranged letters
funny means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an imp is a rascal
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A likeable scamp in a comic cast I adore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' gives SATIC, which the rascal enters before love is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico means congenial and pleasant, easy to like.

clue.text: Spirit put into pretence, not against plot

indicators.note: put into means the spirit is placed inside the other word
not means the letter for against is removed

parts.note: a veneer is a thin show, a pretence
V is short for versus, against
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Spirit hidden in a pretence, not opposed to the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not against' takes V from VENEER, leaving ENEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive or plot it.

clue.text: Disliked going north around cape, cut off

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes round the cape letter
going north in a down clue means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: hated means disliked

explanation.surface: Unpopular explorer heading north around a cape is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to separate, to cut off.

clue.text: Give piercing cry and rock companion

parts.note: scree is loose rock on a slope
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Shriek, and rock your companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To screech is to make a shrill, harsh cry.

clue.text: Misbehave in a court in front of judge

parts.note: being up means appearing before a judge in court

explanation.surface: Misbehave in court in front of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly.

clue.text: Sympathetic treatment covering area in powder

indicators.note: covering means the treatment letters wrap round the area letter

parts.note: TLC is tender loving care

explanation.surface: Gentle care covering an area with powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into talcum powder.
